outcome_detail: $1.5 million settlement to the four plaintiffs, approved by Harris County Commissioners Court in early June 2024 (reported June 4-6, 2024). Constable Alan Rosen had earlier been dismissed as a defendant by a U.S. District Court judge on August 30, 2021.
criminal_detail: The FBI opened an investigation into the Precinct 1 Human Trafficking Unit in 2021 after the lawsuit was filed, with the plaintiffs cooperating; no criminal charges against the accused officers have been publicly reported as of July 2026. The constable's office said an internal affairs investigation found no violations of law or policy.
incident_date_approx: Alleged misconduct during undercover 'bachelor party' sting operations in the years preceding the May 2021 filing (circa 2019-2021)
description: Four current and former female deputies of the Harris County Constable's Office, Precinct 1 — Liz Gomez, Marissa Sanchez, Felicia McKinney and Jassmine Huff — filed a federal lawsuit in May 2021 against Harris County, Constable Alan Rosen, Assistant Chief Chris Gore and Lt. Shane Rigdon. The suit alleged that rookie female deputies recruited to the office's Human Trafficking Unit were subjected to unwanted touching and kissing, molestation and sexual ridicule by intoxicated commanding officers during undercover 'bachelor party' prostitution stings, and that one deputy was sent undercover alone with a man described in the complaint as a known rapist who sexually assaulted her. The suit further alleged that deputies who reported the conduct faced ridicule and retaliation. A federal judge dismissed Rosen from the case in August 2021. Harris County commissioners approved a $1.5 million settlement with the four women in June 2024. The FBI opened an investigation in 2021; no criminal charges have been publicly reported.
notes: Outside strict police-department definition (county constable's office). Constable Alan Rosen was named as a defendant alleged to be complicit but was dismissed from the suit in August 2021 and was not among those accused of committing the assaults.
